notes: Valtz's model manifest. vpipe's own catalogue says how to FETCH and
LOAD a checkpoint; this file adds what Valtz needs to OFFER it: which
capabilities it serves, how much disk and RAM it needs, and how it
ranks against alternatives for the same capability.
disk_gb: measured=true figures are du of a complete download; the
rest are estimates, replaced by the hub listing when first checked.
min_ram_gb: the smallest tier the model is OFFERED on (streamed DiTs
run on 16 GB; see vpipe docs/MODEL-MEMORY.md). rank: higher wins
when several installed models fit the same capability.
auto: what the model field's Auto tries, per modality (image, video,
audio) and op, in priority order; the first this machine can run
(installed, fits, and the engine has its graph) is the pick.
prompting.language: "english" for a model prompted in English only
(the assistant translates a request for it); without it the model reads
Chinese as well, and the assistant keeps the request's language.
families: how Settings > Capabilities lists the models -- a family's
features (video-gen, video-edit, image-gen, image-edit, audio-gen,
helper, video-summary, video-upscale, image-upscale, audio-transcribe),
each checked where a member makes it here, and its members (every
model and resource it runs with), each with the label it is listed
by.
engine.vpipe.sampling (an assistant): the token sampler its chat
decodes with -- vpipe's sampler-select config, the model card's own
recommendation (Qwen's non-thinking one: Valtz runs it without
thinking); without it, greedy.
engine.vpipe.listen (a speech model): the voice detector it needs and
the tagger it lists sound events with when that is installed (DESIGN
§4h). package: the folder a CoreML archive (`file`, a .tar) unpacks
into, beside it, which holds the package its stage loads.
engine.vpipe.steps_fixed: a distilled checkpoint whose schedule is
its own (Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo's sample_sigmas): no scheduler is wired,
the step count is defaults.steps whatever is asked, and Favor's Custom
offers no steps.
engine.vpipe.first_frame / last_frame: a clip model that opens on a
picture (I2VA), and one that also ends on a second (FL2VA: generate-
video's last-keyframe port). prompting.first_last_tag: what its guide
calls the two pictures of such a clip (MiniMax H3's FL2VA: bare
"Picture 1", "Picture 2", unlike I2VA's <Picture 1>).
engine.vpipe.references.seam: a continuation's frames are matched to
the clip they continue at the seam -- vpipe's content-aware-
continuation between the decode and the writer, its config this
object -- against the tail the model was given. Its tone only: the
geometry it measures pairs the pixels, but across a moving shot's
seam it is the camera's motion (apply_geometry false).
engine.vpipe.negative: "conditioner" -- the family's conditioner
emits the negative conditioning on its second output (MOSS-Image: the
empty prompt's, for its CFG), wired to generate-image's negative port
and kept with the conditioning. engine.vpipe.config_shift: the
schedule's shift is taken by the family's config stage (`shift`), not
a scheduler-select -- this its default -- so Custom's shift offers it.

models.name: Qwen3.5 9B
models.notes: OptiQ mixed 4/8-bit, vision tower included, and an MTP draft head (optiq/mtp.safetensors) the chat decodes with. ~19-20 tok/s decode on an M5 16 GB.

models.name: Qwen3.8 27B
models.notes: OptiQ mixed 4/8-bit: 19.4 GB of weights + 0.9 GB vision tower + 0.3 GB MTP head (optiq/mtp.safetensors: the chat decodes with it). The DFlash 2 drafter is trained on Qwen3.8 27B whatever its packing: it drafts for this one too (vpipe checks its layers, width and vocabulary at load). Offered from 32 GB: on a 24 GB M5 Pro the GPU keeps 17.8 GB resident against its 19.7 GB, and a decode paged every token (2026-10-05). The image/video model is unloaded while it runs.

models.name: Qwen3.8 27B (4-bit)
models.notes: Uniform MLX 4-bit (group 64), vision tower in the shards: 16.1 GB. Its conversion drops the MTP head; mlx-community ships it apart (qwen3.8-27b-mtp-4bit, downloaded with it), which vpipe's text-chat decodes with (mtp_model). On a 24 GB M5 Pro (2026-10-05): 24.6 tok/s with the drafter, 17.5 without; 17.7 GB peak. Ranked with the 9B, which comes first: chosen by name (Settings > Agentic Helper, valtzctl assistant). On the Pro with Qwen's sampler: 22.7 tok/s with the drafter, 17.7 without.

models.name: Qwen3.8 27B MTP drafter
models.notes: Qwen3.8 27B's multi-token-prediction head alone (mlx-vlm's qwen3_5_mtp: bare names, true norm weights, a 4-bit fc), split from the model it drafts for. Not a model by itself: qwen3.8-27b-4bit decodes with it.

models.name: Qwen3.8 27B DFlash 2 drafter
models.notes: Inco AI's DFlash 2 block drafter for Qwen3.8 27B (five layers, 2B parameters, bf16 on disk): it drafts a block from the model's hidden states, which the model verifies in one forward (vpipe's text-chat draft_model). Held at 8 bits (~2.2 GB) or 4 bits (~1.3 GB) in memory, beside the model's 17 GB (the OptiQ pack's 20.7): an option, not the default (Settings > Agentic Helper > Drafter). Either 27B -- the 4-bit, the OptiQ pack -- drafts with it.

models.name: Qwen3.8 Flash-Next (uncensored)
models.notes: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a sparse Mixture of Experts that sees (~180B parameters stored: 512 experts a layer, ten read a token, and a 51B-parameter n-gram table), in mlx-community's oQ5e pack of orcarouter's ABLITERATED build -- its safety alignment taken out, so it does what Qwen's own refuses: chosen by name only, never Auto's. 128.6 GB on disk; at least 6.8 GB resident (vpipe's plan with every expert streamed), the routed experts (83 GB) in a cache the size of what is left and the n-gram table (38 GB) read from disk a row at a time -- the drive's speed is the decode's on a Mac that cannot hold them; on 256 GB all but the table load (87 GB wired, 92 GB peak). Its own Lightning MTP head drafts ahead, or -- chosen in Settings > Agentic Helper > Drafter -- the DFlash 2 drafter (vpipe 8d005eca). vpipe 79f954ad. Qwen Community License 1.0.

models.name: Qwen3.8 Flash-Next DFlash 2 drafter
models.notes: Inco AI's DFlash 2 block drafter for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (five layers at its 2560 width, every layer a 2048-token window, bf16 on disk): it reads five of the model's layers -- 5, 15, 25, 35, 45, each averaged over its four residual streams -- drafts a block, and the model checks the block in one pass, keeping the tokens it agrees with: the model's own tokens, faster (vpipe 8d005eca, text-chat draft_model). Held at 8 bits (~0.55 GB and its window caches) or 4 in memory. On vpipe's M4 Pro, the experts cached: 20 tok/s plain, ~31 with it (3.2 tokens a round); a fresh conversation 9.4 against the MTP head's 7.3. On the M5 Ultra (2026-10-21, every expert loaded): 45 tok/s warm, 2.8 a round, against the MTP head's 38-40 (2.5). An option, not the default (Settings > Agentic Helper > Drafter). Apache-2.0.

models.name: Z-Image Turbo
models.notes: 6B DiT, 8 steps. Streams its F32 checkpoint on 16 GB (46 s at 1024^2 on an M5).

models.name: FLUX.3 Image Klein
models.notes: Black Forest Labs' 5.6B flow-map DiT, distilled to 16 steps with no guidance pass: text to image, and edits from up to ten references. Pictures up to 4096 x 4096 (any side from 64): a 4096-pixel square takes over an hour, the VAE decoded in exact tiles. It reads a full scene caption -- medium, scene, light, camera, each subject placed in the frame -- and an edit as an expanded instruction: the change, its effects, what stays. BFL's upsampler wrote its training captions; Enhance writes them here. Its text encoder is Qwen3-VL-4B, text only; its VAE and preview are FLUX.2's. Compressing packs its DiT (11.1 GB) at 8 or 4 bits; the encoder stays as published.

models.name: MOSS-Image SFT

options.label: Guidance

models.notes: OpenMOSS's 5B single-stream DiT, fine-tuned from MOSS-Image Base for clearer text grouping and layout: text to image, words in the picture in English and Chinese (prompts in natural language, tags, or a JSON layout). 50 steps at CFG 3 against the empty prompt, two forwards a step (its block 22 skipped in the negative): Fine runs them, Med 30, Fast 18. Its text encoder is the full Qwen3.5-9B (16.8 GB, bf16); the model streams, so a 16 GB Mac runs it. Its VAE (FLUX.2's small decoder) and preview are FLUX.2's. Compressing packs its DiT (10.2 GB) at 8 or 4 bits (plain: its SITU feed-forward takes no AWQ); the encoder stays as published.

models.name: FLUX.2 [klein] 9B
models.notes: Multi-reference edit. vpipe's prepare-klein-9b-4bit graph quantizes it to 4-bit (12 GB) after download. Prompted in English: the assistant translates for it.

models.name: Fibo 2.0 Edit Turbo
models.notes: Bria's 8B DiT (Z-Image's block, a Perceiver squeezing the words into 256-512 gist tokens, five blocks cross-attending their own text bundle), distilled to edit in 4 steps with no guidance: an instruction, or a JSON object with an edit_instruction and a structured_caption of the result; up to five pictures, named image_1, image_2, ... Editing only (Bria's text-to-image model is Fibo 2.0 Dev, not run). Its text encoder Qwen3-VL-4B reads the words and the pictures (thumbnailed to 768 a side); fifteen of its layers condition the DiT. Trained at about one megapixel: each picture is cropped to the trained size of its shape (1024 x 1024, 1152 x 864, 1248 x 832, 1424 x 800, 1568 x 672, ...), the result at the first's. Its VAE is FLUX.2's (its int8 in Custom and Fast); its live preview FLUX.2's TAE (FLUX klein's). Streams on 16 GB: a 1024^2 edit 101 s at int8 Per Token on a base M5, 100 s dense on an M4 Pro (vpipe 17c53d63). Gated on Hugging Face; CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial.

models.name: Qwen-Image 2.1
models.notes: One checkpoint for generate and edit; native RGBA (straight alpha) output.

models.name: Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo
models.notes: Qwen's own distillation of Qwen-Image 2.1 to 8 steps: the same DiT, VL encoder and RGBA VAE, generate and edit alike. Its schedule is in its files (model_index.json's sample_sigmas, dynamic shifting off) and vpipe runs it as written, so no scheduler is wired and the step count is the checkpoint's. Not the Turbo LoRA (qwen-image-21-turbo), which speeds up the base model.

models.notes: FlashVSR+ with sparse attention on every layer: slower than Turbo, a stream taking more memory, its makers' pick where the quality comes first. Shares Turbo's decoder and VAE (one download of them).

models.name: TAE (MiniMax H3)
models.notes: Temporal: decodes the clip's own frame count. Published in madebyollin's taehv GitHub repo beside taew2_1.

models.name: MiniMax H3 Turbo LoRA (6-step)
models.notes: Few-step distillation of the FL2VA partition (v4, step 600, EMA): video and audio in 4-8 steps, applied at run time at scale 1.

models.name: MiniMax H3 HyperFlow
models.notes: Video Rebirth's 8-step flow-map self-distillation: the adapter brings its own sigma grid, so the step count is its 8. Each forward is ~9% slower than the base model's. Takes the adapter slot the Turbo LoRA would.

models.name: MiniMax H3 VDN linear branch
models.notes: VideoDeltaNet hybrid attention (stage DMD): a windowed softmax over nearby frames plus a linear delta-rule recurrence over the rest, a second checkpoint beside the DiT. Worth it on long clips at large sizes; replaces Sol-Attn on the blocks it covers.

models.name: MiniMax H3 Image VAE
models.notes: Mamad8's single-latent-frame decoder: H3 decodes one frame as a still with it (vpipe's vae-decode takes it for a one-frame latent).

models.name: MiniMax H3 TaoMate adapter
models.notes: TaoLive's 3-step adapter for the FL2VA partition (step-3000 generator EMA, rank 128, a PEFT adapter folder) -- the adapter of a streaming METHOD, not a few-step LoRA: the base model writes the soundtrack, the adapter the video in chunks against a clean K/V cache (vpipe's taomate; Favor's TaoMate). Text to clip only, in whole 5-second requests; its cache is kept on disk. An alternative method in Favor's Custom: no preset turns it on.

models.name: MiniMax H3 FL2VA 4-step LoRA
models.notes: lightx2v's 4-step Turbo for FL2VA (v1.2, 768p), distilled at video shift 6.

models.name: MiniMax H3 Ref2VA 4-step LoRA
models.notes: lightx2v's 4-step Turbo for the Ref2VA partition (v0.1, ComfyUI keys).

models.name: MiniMax H3 FL2VA 8-step LoRA
models.notes: lightx2v's 8-step Turbo for FL2VA (v1.0, 768p, video shift 6).

models.name: MiniMax H3 Ref2VA 8-step LoRA
models.notes: lightx2v's 8-step Turbo for the Ref2VA partition (v1.0, 768p).

models.name: Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo LoRA
models.notes: Viggle's 6-step turbo for Qwen-Image 2.1 (v0.2.1, rank 128: what upstream's ComfyUI workflows load).

models.name: Qwen-Image 2.1 prompt rewriters
models.notes: QwenLM's own instructions for writing Qwen-Image 2.1 prompts and edit instructions, which Enhance then follows in place of Valtz's own guide. Under the Qwen Research License: for NON-COMMERCIAL use only (its LICENSE is downloaded beside them). Fetched from QwenLM's GitHub repository, pinned to one commit.

models.name: Qwen3-ASR 1.7B
models.notes: Qwen's speech recognizer, 8-bit MLX: speech to text in 52 languages and dialects, the language found by itself. The larger and more accurate of the two.

models.name: Qwen3-ASR 0.6B
models.notes: Qwen's speech recognizer, 8-bit MLX: the smaller and faster of the two.

models.name: Silero VAD v6
models.notes: A voice activity detector (CoreML): where speech starts and stops, so the speech model hears each stretch whole and each line is timed.

models.name: BEATs AS2M
models.notes: Microsoft's audio tagger (CoreML): the sounds heard -- music, laughter, a dog, rain -- by AudioSet's 527 labels, ten seconds at a time. Optional: with it, a transcript lists the sound events.

models.name: BS-RoFormer Resurrection (vocals)
models.notes: A Band-Split RoPE Transformer (MSST's format: a torch checkpoint beside its YAML) trained to take the VOICE out of a song: the vocals, and the accompaniment as what is left. 51M parameters, under 1 GB of memory whatever the song's length; a 3:34 song in 37-55 s. Its repository states NO license: fetchable, not shipped -- decide before using what it makes beyond your own listening.

models.name: BS-RoFormer Resurrection (instrumental)
models.notes: The same network trained on the ACCOMPANIMENT: the cleaner instrumental (a karaoke track), the vocals as what is left. A little slower than the vocals model (finer time steps). Its repository states NO license.
